ops.new_text: Within the frozen 20-source corpus, the closest architectural comparators are the approximate-candidate-to-rigorous-output separation represented by Hoffman et al. and the production-artifact-to-independent-checking pattern represented by Hales et al. The shared features are an untrusted producer, a stable evidence object, explicit predicates, and a checker that need not reproduce the producer's search. P33's narrower addition is a mathematical owner-semantics layer for two surface-specific producers: the common record distinguishes full-group conjugacy, maximal roots and primitivity, external inversion pairing, self-reciprocity, repetitions, cutoff disposition, termination, and completeness while permitting different internal mathematics. This is a closest-work comparison only within the bounded frozen corpus. No external novelty search was performed, so the comparison establishes neither field-general firstness nor priority, and the manuscript makes no such claim.

The field-facing method was a closed-corpus evidence synthesis. It first froze the two source-locked surfaces, unit-speed physical base-geodesic time, \(b=1/2\), the signed-field even subsequence, the inverse-paired primitive-owner rule, \(\Lambda=21/10\), the result taxonomy, and fail-closed states. It then screened a bounded corpus of 20 retained sources and recorded, for each record, identity, verification status, admissible use, exclusion boundary, and locator status. Source-effect rows were aligned by mathematical function and synthesized into object, candidate-generation, conjugacy, root-decision, owner-semantics, rigorous-predicate, and producer-checker themes. Architectural inferences were separated from literature-supported facts, and adversarial, citation-integrity, ethical, and editorial checks were retained as provenance rather than as scientific evidence. The complete numbered workflow history and its checkpoints remain in the repository path manifest; they are not used as the reader-facing explanation of the method.

The independent-validator contract remains prospective. Its trust graph has producer nodes BP and CP, adapter nodes \(A_{\mathrm{BP}}\) and \(A_{\mathrm{CP}}\), a byte parser \(V_{\mathrm{parse}}\), predicate kernels \(V_{\mathrm{pred}}\), a fixture-oracle node \(O\), theorem-encoding records, external libraries, and accountable implementers. In any future implementation, the intended trusted computing base would be limited to the then-frozen schema and proof-type registry, canonical-byte and digest rules, \(V_{\mathrm{parse}}\), \(V_{\mathrm{pred}}\), and explicitly disclosed theorem encodings; producer status labels and search code would remain outside it. Sharing the schema, digest specification, or a disclosed general-purpose arithmetic or cryptographic library is allowed. Sharing a theorem encoding, adapter helper, or fixture-generation utility must be disclosed and prevents that component from being described as independently implemented. Reuse of producer decision code inside \(V_{\mathrm{pred}}\), a mutable or producer-derived expected-output oracle, an undisclosed dependency, or one hidden implementation serving as both producer and checker is disqualifying. Every future node must carry an accountable implementer, source-tree digest, build-environment digest, and build SHA-256. At present \texttt{BP}, \texttt{CP}, both adapters, the checker, and an independently authored oracle are \texttt{UNAVAILABLE\_COMPONENT\_NOT\_IMPLEMENTED}; consequently no build hash is invented and validator independence is not established. Failure at parsing, proof dispatch, cutoff replay, conjugacy, root, inversion, reciprocity, repetition, uniqueness, termination, coverage, or unresolved-record checks must yield rejected, bounded-incomplete, or not-evaluable status rather than acceptance.

The paper-level common contract is \path{P33-OWNER-CERT/1} with proof registry \path{P33-PROOF-TYPES/1}. Its closed allowed top-level field set is \path{schema_version}, \path{proof_registry_digest}, \path{surface_id}, \path{producer_id}, \path{run_id}, \path{record_type}, \path{candidate_id}, \path{producer_representation}, \path{enumeration_provenance}, \path{oriented_class_digest}, \path{primitive_root_digest}, \path{root_exponent}, \path{inverse_class_digest}, \path{owner_id}, \path{owner_member_digests}, \path{cutoff}, \path{cutoff_disposition}, \path{proof_type}, \path{proof_payload}, \path{input_digest}, \path{theorem_version_digest}, \path{implementation_digest}, \path{correction_provenance_digest}, \path{clock_id}, \path{subtype_id}, \path{owner_rule_id}, \path{termination_witness}, \path{coverage_digest}, \path{unresolved_count}, \path{validator_version}, \path{validator_digest}, \path{fixture_set_digest}, \path{predicate_decisions}, \path{rejected_incompatibilities}, and \path{state}. The record family determines the mandatory subset described in the preceding schema table; unlisted fields, missing mandatory fields, or unrecognized enum values fail closed. The closed \path{record_type} enum is \path{run_header}, \path{candidate}, \path{conjugacy}, \path{root}, \path{inversion}, \path{owner}, \path{repetition}, \path{termination}, \path{coverage}, or \path{validation}; \path{surface_id} is \path{BOLZA-SOURCE-LOCK} or \path{NAZARENKO-EXP-OCTAGON-G2}. The closed \path{state} enum is \path{declared}, \path{parsed}, \path{predicate_checked}, \path{accepted}, \path{rejected}, \path{bounded_incomplete}, or \path{not_evaluable}. The proof registry admits only \path{exact_conjugator}, \path{canonical_conjugacy_normal_form}, \path{maximal_root}, \path{no_proper_power}, \path{systolic_primitive}, \path{exact_cutoff_comparison}, \path{exact_trace_comparison}, \path{conjugacy_to_inverse}, \path{termination_measure}, and \path{coverage_replay}; each payload must name its input digests and supply the exact witness consumed by the correspondingly named predicate. State moves are \path{declared} to \path{parsed} to \path{predicate_checked} and then to exactly one terminal state; only the checker may derive the final move. A complete run is rejected if any conjugacy, root, cutoff, inverse, owner, termination, or coverage disposition is unresolved; if a proof type cannot be dispatched, the run is \path{not_evaluable}. A primitive record cannot have exponent greater than one, a repetition cannot mint an owner distinct from its primitive root's owner, and a self-reciprocal record requires separate conjugacy-to-inverse evidence plus its external inverse link. Failed termination or coverage, a missing correction binding, duplicate canonical owner IDs, digest drift, or an unrecognized proof type precludes acceptance. This closes the semantic contract at manuscript level but does not assert that a producer, schema file, proof registry file, adapter, fixture, or validator has been implemented or run.

\textbf{Surface-specific population-completeness procedure.} The prospective BP contract must consume the exact source-locked Bolza presentation in \path{papers/28-bolza-magnetic-flow/results/round4_bolza_group_certificate.json}, SHA-256 \url{e3e6c486c66116dc6fe9fdd054c2fce9d4b1a58318f56d1656f6db168c807eca}; the prospective CP contract must consume \texttt{NAZARENKO-EXP-OCTAGON-G2} from \path{papers/28-bolza-magnetic-flow/results/round7_nonarithmetic_control_matrices.json}, SHA-256 \url{a900749b6905a5f324c2e2670363ec1bc9480481f3f5aa1240ed0ebbee55e6ca}. BP's bounded domain is empty only after exact replay of \(\operatorname{sys}(S_{\mathrm{Bolza}})>21/10\); failure or digest drift stops as \texttt{UPSTREAM\_REPLAY\_CONTRADICTION}. CP's bounded domain is the exact identity-connected centre-guard component from the frozen certificate \path{papers/28-bolza-magnetic-flow/results/round8_control_finite_ball_certificate.json}, SHA-256 \url{c1bf68a8a1485665680dba01d0012fb691c7ca1a795e36334639e34bbbdbcb1f}. Its order is FIFO breadth-first traversal from the identity through \(g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3,g_0^{-1},g_1^{-1},g_2^{-1},g_3^{-1}\), with exact normalized-state deduplication; each neighbour is classified by the exact centre guard \(\lvert\alpha\rvert^2\leq20000\), and final streams are lexicographically sorted by canonical state bytes. Cutoff admission is always the exact comparison \(\ell(g)\leq21/10\), never a rounded decimal. BP terminates on a verified strict systole replay; CP terminates only when the FIFO queue is empty and every outgoing edge from every included state has an included or rejected disposition. Coverage binds the sorted included and rejected streams, theorem and input digests, cutoff, and a complete unresolved ledger; the accepted upstream stream digests are \url{814f72badce2cc90e8e26edc2a7db18d52c4c334c0f5dfc5bf7d8e4a90dcf545} and \url{3017c21285daad5a1173b076c9b5700975f67cdbbdaa8a6218e80d4bc89da6f4}. An independent checker must reconstruct the bound and both stream digests; nonzero unresolved count yields bounded-incomplete or not-evaluable status. These artifacts fix input bytes but do not discharge the future obligations to bind exact theorem and algorithm versions, prove applicability, and emit checkable proof payloads rather than status labels. This paragraph fixes an executable contract from accepted upstream bytes; it executes no producer, replay, owner quotient, or census here.

The frozen specialization is \(u=a=e^{-1/10}\), \(\alpha=\pi/4\), \(x=u^2=e^{-1/5}\), \(\Delta=(1-u^2)(2u^2-1)\), and \(N=-\Delta^{-1/2}\). Its proof-bearing ordered generators are
\[
 g_0=N\begin{pmatrix}u&u^2+i(1-u^2)\\u^2-i(1-u^2)&u\end{pmatrix},\quad
 g_1=N\begin{pmatrix}u&(1-u^2)+iu^2\\(1-u^2)-iu^2&u\end{pmatrix},
\]
with \(R=\operatorname{diag}(e^{i\pi/4},e^{-i\pi/4})\), \(g_2=Rg_0R^{-1}\), and \(g_3=Rg_1R^{-1}\), under the presentation
\[
 \langle g_0,g_1,g_2,g_3\mid g_0g_1^{-1}g_2g_3^{-1}g_0^{-1}g_1g_2^{-1}g_3=I\rangle .
\]
The producer input uses \(\ell(g)=2\operatorname{arcosh}(|\operatorname{tr}g|/2)\), exact admission \(\ell(g)\leq21/10\), and the finite-domain centre guard \(\lvert\alpha_g\rvert^2\leq20000\). The canonical generator-object bytes are \path{papers/28-bolza-magnetic-flow/results/round7_nonarithmetic_control_matrices.json}, SHA-256 \url{a900749b6905a5f324c2e2670363ec1bc9480481f3f5aa1240ed0ebbee55e6ca}; the bound finite certificate is \path{papers/28-bolza-magnetic-flow/results/round8_control_finite_ball_certificate.json}, SHA-256 \url{c1bf68a8a1485665680dba01d0012fb691c7ca1a795e36334639e34bbbdbcb1f}. CP must consume those exact values and digests. This is a transcription of accepted upstream locks, not a new replay, theorem, or census.

Package B fixes owner semantics across the producer boundary. Let \(d(g)\) be the canonical digest of an oriented full-group conjugacy class after its conjugacy predicate has passed, and let \(d(g^{-1})\) be computed independently under the same rule. If a separate conjugacy-to-inverse proof passes, the self-reciprocal owner has the deduplicated singleton member list \([d(g)]\), cardinality one, and an inverse link to itself. Otherwise the owner has the two distinct member digests \([\min(d(g),d(g^{-1})),\max(d(g),d(g^{-1}))]\), cardinality two, in byte-lexicographic order, with reciprocal inverse links. The owner identifier is
\[
 \operatorname{SHA256}(\texttt{P33-owner-v1}\mathbin{\|\!\|}\texttt{surface-id}\mathbin{\|\!\|}\texttt{member-count}\mathbin{\|\!\|}\texttt{ordered-member-bytes}),
\]
where each separator and field encoding follows the canonical-byte contract. Duplicate candidate rows are removed before this derivation and cannot change the member list or identifier. A repetition records its primitive-root digest and the already derived root owner identifier; it never mints an owner. Equal length, trace, word, homology, or literal matrix data cannot set self-reciprocity or merge owners. These rules fix membership, deduplication, inverse links, and owner IDs without asserting that any owner has been computed.

The following manuscript-local traces are synthetic conformance examples, not surface records, executable fixture files, validator runs, or census outcomes. In the valid trace, a BP private payload tagged \path{exact_trace_comparison} and a CP private payload tagged \path{canonical_conjugacy_normal_form} are each mapped by their adapters to the common fields \path{surface_id}, \path{run_id=synthetic}, \path{candidate_id}, oriented-class, root, inverse, and owner digests, \path{cutoff=21/10}, proof type, coverage digest, and \path{unresolved_count=0}. The parser accepts only canonical bytes, the registry dispatches each recognized tag to its stated predicate, all required links and digests are present, and the checker alone moves both records from \path{declared} through \path{parsed} and \path{predicate_checked} to the closed terminal state \path{accepted}; its interpretation is limited in prose to a synthetic fixture. In the invalid trace, a BP-shaped record omits \path{inverse_class_digest} and therefore moves to \path{rejected:missing_inverse_link}; a CP-shaped record supplies \path{proof_type=unknown_demo} and therefore moves to \path{not_evaluable:unrecognized_proof_type}. Neither branch may be repaired from producer labels, approximate equality, or another record's payload. The examples expose the end-to-end adapter, predicate, state-transition, and fail-closed semantics while carrying no scientific input or result.

Canonical records use UTF-8 in NFC form, no byte-order mark, LF line endings, byte-lexicographically ordered object keys, prescribed array order, and no insignificant whitespace. Integers use unsigned or explicitly signed base-10 strings without leading zeros; a rational uses the canonical byte-order object \texttt{\{den,num\}}, where \texttt{den} is positive, \texttt{num} is signed, and the two integers are coprime; floating-point numbers, NaN, infinities, duplicate keys, and unknown fields are forbidden. The record digest is SHA-256 of the ASCII domain prefix \texttt{P33-OWNER-CERT}, one zero byte, the schema version, one zero byte, the proof-registry digest, one zero byte, and the canonical record bytes. Records are ordered by \texttt{surface\_id}, \texttt{record\_type}, and record digest; owner members use the deterministic rule stated below. Compatibility requires exact equality of both \texttt{schema\_version} and \texttt{proof\_registry\_digest}. A migration is never implicit: it must have its own version and digest, a total source-to-target transformation contract, declared failure states, preserved source bytes, and complete parser, predicate, owner, coverage, and digest revalidation of every transformed record. No execution digest is emitted here, and these byte rules do not claim that an external schema file or validator exists.

At \(\Lambda=21/10\), P33 treats both cutoff directions as unverified inherited assumptions, not as a design fact or a new census. The target direction is conditional: if a separately frozen, passage-adequate Bolza source-and-proof record is valid and its exact strict-systole comparison replays successfully, then the below-cutoff candidate universe is empty. The control direction is also conditional: if the separately frozen control certificate and primitive witness are valid and replay successfully, then at least one below-cutoff primitive owner must be represented. P33 has not closed either source-to-proof chain at passage level, so claim-to-passage faithfulness remains \texttt{INCONCLUSIVE}. These conditionals may parameterize only fail-closed producer obligations and upstream-contradiction checks; they do not establish an empty-versus-nonempty comparison, distinguish arithmetic from nonarithmetic geometry, or license a formal A0 verdict, A1 closure, positive arithmetic A2 status, or Route-B conclusion. The cutoff remains target-blind and must not be retuned after the inherited directions became known.
